recap.question: You are auditing an AI-native recommendation API that currently relies only on static unit tests and offline Precision@K metrics. Your gap analysis reveals that the system frequently fails when real users request rare categories. Which improvement best addresses this evaluation gap?
options: Increase code coverage of the API route handlers to 100%.
Integrate behavioral test suites using edge-case inputs alongside online slice-based evaluation metrics.
Measure latency using load testing tools without changing model evaluation metrics.
Switch the recommendation algorithm database from PostgreSQL to Redis.
recap.explanation: Addressing coverage gaps in AI services requires behavioral testing targeted at edge cases and slice-based metrics to evaluate sub-population performance beyond aggregate precision.

questions.question: Why are traditional assertion-based unit tests insufficient for evaluating AI-native systems?
options: System-centric testing only measures underlying hardware usage rather than software behavior.
AI models do not use standard programming languages or software engineering pipelines.
AI-native systems exhibit nondeterminism and data drift, making fixed input-output assertions fragile.
Model training completely replaces all traditional software source code in production.
questions.explanation: AI-native systems introduce non-determinism, data drift, and model evolution, which makes fixed deterministic assertion testing inadequate.

questions.question: When testing an ML model function without ground-truth labels (the oracle problem), which mechanism verifies logic by checking if relations between transformed inputs and outputs hold?
questions.explanation: Metamorphic testing addresses the test oracle problem by checking whether expected relations hold between outputs when specific transformations are applied to inputs.

questions.question: Which integration testing technique ensures that data passing between components in an ML pipeline adheres to expected data types, values, and structural bounds?
questions.explanation: Schema validation inspects pipeline data flow to guarantee that inputs and outputs meet structural contracts before execution reaches downstream models.

questions.question: A diagnostic AI outputs probability scores. Which metric measures how closely these predicted confidence probabilities reflect the true frequency of outcomes?
questions.explanation: Calibration error evaluates whether a model's predicted confidence probabilities accurately match observed empirical frequencies.

questions.question: An online AI service must meet an SLA requirement of serving 100 requests per second with response times under 50ms. Which pair of system metrics monitors this?
questions.explanation: Latency measures per-request response time while throughput tracks request handling capacity, directly mapping to production operational SLAs.

questions.question: A team implements integration schema validation and model calibration checks for an NLP system. Which quality gap remains unaddressed by this evaluation setup?
options: Data type correctness between pipeline stages
Robustness against perturbed or adversarial inputs
questions.explanation: Schema checks cover pipeline integration and calibration checks cover model confidence, but neither tests model behavior against adversarial perturbations.

questions.question: A RAG pipeline shows good retrieval accuracy but slow overall response times. Which evaluation strategy best isolates whether the delay comes from the retrieval component or the generator model?
options: Compute overall corpus perplexity instead of F1 score.
Benchmark latency independently for vector retrieval versus LLM token generation.
Add schema validation to the generator output parser.
Apply metamorphic transformations to the vector database index.
questions.explanation: Separating system metrics (retrieval latency) from model generation latency isolates component-level performance bottlenecks in a multi-stage RAG architecture.
